_README: The grammar of a journalist-query digest email, kept in data rather than in
code so it can be corrected the day a provider changes its layout without
touching the filtering or drafting logic.
This grammar was NOT built from a captured sample. Nobody in this account is
so it is written to the labelled-field layout SOS and HARO digests use, and
it is written to FAIL LOUDLY rather than to guess.
That last part is the whole design. The dangerous failure here is not a
parser that breaks; it is a parser that returns zero queries from a digest
full of them and gets reported as 'nothing relevant today'. So a message body
that yields no parseable block is a NAMED STOP called UNPARSEABLE_DIGEST that
names the provider and quotes the first lines it could not read. A quiet day
and a broken parser must never look the same.
